extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, area chairs/action editors, and PC chairs for *ACL conferences (ACL, NAACL, EACL) and the TACL journal
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and standards governing anonymization, preprint handling, reviewer behavior, citation, and comparison expectations for submissions to *ACL conferences and the TACL journal. Includes procedures for reviewers and guidance on how to treat refereed publications versus preprints and contemporaneous work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions must be anonymized
rubrics_metrics.description: '*ACL conferences and TACL require that submissions be anonymized.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that are not anonymized may be rejected. The page notes that parts of the policy applied to papers submitted before Jan 12, 2024 and that authors are cautioned against extensive advertising; authors should make their submitted paper 'as anonymous as possible.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity period rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission will not be considered anonymized if the authors post (or update) a non-anonymized preprint version within an anonymity period lasting from 1 month before the submission deadline until the time of notification (or withdrawal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-anonymized preprint is posted/updated during the anonymity period the submission will be treated as non-anonymized and submissions will be rejected if not properly anonymized. The anonymity period definition and the requirement to avoid non-anonymized posts/updates are central enforcement points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymized preprints allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymized preprints within the anonymity period are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is currently only possible on certain platforms; ACL may consider using such a platform for all submissions in the future. The policy distinguishes between anonymized and non-anonymized preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling existing non-anonymized preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-anonymized preprints posted before the anonymity period are allowed, but authors are encouraged to wait to post them until after the anonymity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-anonymized preprint version exists at submission time, authors must declare its existence at submission, should not cite it, and are asked not to publicize it further during the anonymity period — the submitted paper should still be as anonymous as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited permitted updates to preprints (name corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL explicitly allows updates to preprints, at all times, for the sole purpose of correcting people’s names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the change falls within the required anonymous period of a conference, the PC Chairs should be notified of the correction. The restriction is intended to prevent authors from circumventing the rules by 'flag planting' with placeholder versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of preprint for policy purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of 'preprint' is understood broadly to refer to any non-refereed paper posted online, including but not limited to preprint servers such as arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule applies only to preprints that authors post themselves (not to non-refereed proceedings volumes, etc.). This clarifies scope of what counts as a preprint under the anonymization rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct regarding author identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be instructed not to actively try to discover the identity of the authors and not to let any suspicion or knowledge of author identity affect their judgment of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should not prevent reviewers from searching for related work, but they should take special care and postpone such searches until after they have read the paper completely and formed an initial impression of it. The intent is to preserve double-blind review merit while allowing literature checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when reviewer uncovers or suspects author identity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer nevertheless uncovers the identity of the authors (or believes they can identify the authors for other reasons), they should inform the area chair or action editor (but not other reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that knowledge of identity can be considered by decision-makers (area chair/action editor) when making the final acceptance decision, while avoiding contaminating other reviewers' independent judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer disclosure of outside knowledge (post-Jan 12, 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: After January 12, 2024, ACL reviewing procedures will explicitly ask reviewers to disclose any outside knowledge they may have about a submitted paper, and will take this information into account when assigning and using reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page indicates a new procedural change: reviewers will be asked to disclose outside knowledge and this disclosure will influence assignment and use of reviews. Further details are referenced in a linked policy note.

rubrics_metrics.name: General citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should in principle cite and compare to all relevant prior work, regardless of when and how that work was presented to the community, and must credit work that influenced them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching rule; the page then provides two important qualifications (priority of refereed publications and treatment of very recent/contemporaneous work) which modulate expectations in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of refereed publications over preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: For citation, refereed publications take priority over preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to cite all refereed publications relevant to their submission, but may be excused for not knowing about all unpublished work (especially recently posted and/or not widely cited preprints). If a preprint has been superseded by a refereed publication, the refereed publication should be cited in addition to or instead of the preprint version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of contemporaneous work (less than 3 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers (whether refereed or not) appearing less than 3 months before the submission deadline should be considered contemporaneous to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relieves authors from the obligation to make detailed comparisons that require additional experimentation and/or in-depth analysis, but they are still expected to cite and discuss contemporaneous work to the degree feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment consequences and reviewer guidance on missing citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to cite relevant prior work or failure to compare to (non-contemporaneous) empirical results may affect the assessment of a submission regardless of how the prior work was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, reviewers should give authors the benefit of the doubt in cases where the work appears in preprints with no corresponding refereed publication, especially recent and/or not widely cited preprints. In such cases, reviewers should point authors to the non-cited work (so they can discuss it in the camera-ready version) but not penalize the authors for missing the citation.
